title: Merritt's Chicago band personnel and singer Lou King
summary: Merritt names his Chicago drummer, bass, piano, reeds and banjo players, Henry and Gordon Paulyat on trombone, and says Lou King was an entertainer who sang and recorded with them.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were some of the other fellas you were with in Chicago when you made the records? Well... I don't remember that.

I believe I got them in that scrapbook. Oh, that's real. We'll still find all that. Look it up, sir. I got a picture of my whole band in this scrapbook. Oh, that's good, yeah. But I don't believe the names are in there. Well, we'll check with you. Well, now, my drummer was Bill Paley. Bill Paley, you want to put it down? Yeah, and we'll have it on the tape here anyway. We'll have it, yeah. We've got it on the tape, don't we? Bill Paley was my drummer. Norman Vanhoek was my bass man. Sousaphone. Maury Friedman was my piano man. Uh, Raleigh the Foe. Yeah, I know him. And Willie Krieger was my two clarinets and sax man. And they're both on the record? Yeah. And Franz Piper was my banjo man.

And Gordon Paulyat, when I put a show in there, he was on trombone. And Gordon Paulyat, when I put a show in there, he was on trombone. And I couldn't read and I had to put a show in there. And I had to put a violin player, and a man that doubled on trumpet, so he could carry the lead, see? And I was directing the band.
Who was Lou King by the way?
